an0776.user: Footwear, blended Meta + Google, spend ₹19.5L last 30 days (post-iOS). Quick question — Meta's dashboard says my ROAS is 3.4 but Shopify last-click says 1.9. Why are they so far apart and which one do I actually believe?

You're asking which dashboard is right, but the honest answer is: neither, and you'll go in circles trying to referee them. They measure different things and they're both biased.

Meta's 3.4 is built on modelled conversions and a 7-day-click (often 1-day-view) attribution window — post-iOS it estimates a lot, and it claims credit for any sale it touched, so it over-counts. Shopify last-click 1.9 only credits the final click before purchase, so it hands all the glory to Google/branded/direct and under-counts Meta's real upper-funnel pull. The true number sits somewhere between 1.9 and 3.4 — and no setting will make the two ever agree, because they're answering different questions.

So stop trying to pick a winner. The mechanism here is attribution itself, not your campaigns.

The lever: anchor on blended CAC — total spend ÷ actual new customers from Shopify. On ₹19.5L, if Shopify shows you, say, 1,100 genuinely new customers, that's a blended CAC of ~₹1,773 — one honest number you can manage to month over month, immune to which platform is bragging. Set a target blended CAC and a target new-customer count and steer by those.

Caveat: 'new customers' has to mean first-time buyers, not all orders — strip repeat purchasers out or blended CAC flatters you. Get that definition clean and the dashboard war stops mattering.
